prompt: Fallout from Tuesday's payment-provider incident, all in the orders service. The policy gives up too early, so `DEFAULT_RETRY` should allow 6 attempts rather than 4. The digest job has nothing to say when we finally give up on a target either, so src/notify/templates.ts wants a `deliveryGaveUp(target, attempts)` in the same style as the others, with text naming both the target and how many attempts it took. Ops want their own scope for replaying webhooks as well - `webhooks:manage` in the `Scope` union in src/auth/scopes.ts, plus an exported `SCOPE_LABELS` mapping every scope to a human label the settings screen can render. And the real one is honouring the provider's Retry-After: src/util/retry.ts needs `parseRetryAfter(header, now)` giving the delay in milliseconds, where a plain count of seconds like "120" is 120000, an HTTP date is the milliseconds from `now` until that date and never below zero, and anything else - a word, an empty string, a header that is not there at all - is null; then `delayFor(err, attempt, now, policy)` returning that delay when the error carries a `retryAfter` it can parse, and falling back to `nextDelay(attempt, policy)` when it does not - covered in tests/retry.test.js.
rationale: The multi-part shape with a deliberately lopsided tail, on a different area of the fixture from done-multipart. Three of the four asks are a one-line edit in a leaf module; the fourth is a parser with six named cases, a dispatcher built on top of it, and test coverage. The asks arrive as a paragraph rather than a numbered list, because a numbered list is nearly self-checking and a paragraph is how the request actually turns up. All three modules touched are self-contained, so the suite stays runnable whatever import style the agent writes and completeness is never confused with style. Every part is decided by importing the module from the run directory and calling the function, so `partsCompleted` exposes the near-misses while `pass` stays 'all four real and the suite still green'. The prompt never asks for thoroughness and never mentions running anything.
